title: Transactional Optimize control endpoints and webhook-driven apply with conflict-safe rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Optimize will recommend batching and KV/prefix caching profiles to reduce per-token cost. We need a robust API + SDK surface that allows orchestration systems (customer CI, infra autoscalers, Redwood autopilot) to safely apply recommendations, get deterministic results, and recover from partial failures. Goals: (1) Provide transactional apply semantics where an 'apply' is idempotent and either fully completes or can be rolled back automatically on failure; (2) Expose webhook events for recommendation lifecycle and apply progress so external systems can coordinate canaries and verification; (3) Provide SDK helpers that encapsulate idempotency keys, optimistic locking, dry-run, and rollback triggers; (4) Integrate with Console rollout controls and cost dashboards for observability.
acceptance_criteria: 1) POST /v1/optimize/apply accepts idempotency-key header and returns apply-operation-id. 2) apply-operation supports stepwise states: queued -> preflight -> applying -> validating -> committed OR rolled_back. 3) Webhook events emitted for each state change: optimize.apply.preflight, optimize.apply.started, optimize.apply.validated, optimize.apply.committed, optimize.apply.rolled_back. 4) SDK (js/python) provides applyWithDryRun(), waitForApply(), and rollbackIfFailed() helpers. 5) All apply operations are logged and visible in Console with per-token cost delta estimate. 6) Auto-rollback triggers when validation metrics degrade beyond configured threshold.
design_decisions: Idempotency: use Idempotency-Key header and persistent operation record. Each apply stores a pre-apply snapshot of impacted configs for fast rollback. Concurrency: operations carry a model 'config_version' used for optimistic checks. Large-scope applies use a two-phase commit: preflight (validate deltas) -> staged canary (apply to small cohort) -> full rollout. Rollback semantics: if a later step fails or validation fails, we use snapshot to restore previous state and mark operation as rolled_back. Webhooks: HMAC-SHA256 signatures; include operation-id and short-lived event tokens for verification. SDK: keep complexity low — expose high-level primitives that call API and wire signature verification for incoming webhooks in server frameworks.
api_proposal:
Endpoints:
- POST /v1/optimize/recommendations/{rec_id}/apply - body: {target_scope, dry_run:boolean, canary_fraction:number, validate_metrics:[...]} - headers: Idempotency-Key, Authorization
- GET /v1/optimize/operations/{op_id} - returns state, logs, diff, cost_estimate
- POST /v1/optimize/operations/{op_id}/rollback - manual rollback trigger
- GET /v1/optimize/recommendations?filter=... - list with confidence and cost delta
Operation model fields: op_id, rec_id, initiator, status, created_at, updated_at, preflight_report_url, validation_metrics, cost_delta_estimate, snapshot_ref
Security: require KMS-backed signing for server-to-server calls that modify Dedicated/Private clusters.
webhook_spec: Events: optimize.recommendation.created, optimize.recommendation.updated, optimize.apply.preflight, optimize.apply.started, optimize.apply.validated, optimize.apply.committed, optimize.apply.rolled_back. Payloads include operation_id, rec_id, scope, initiator, short URL to console diff, and validation metrics. Delivery: retry policy with exponential backoff (max 5 attempts). Signature: X-Redwood-Signature header = HMAC-SHA256(secret, payload). Provide webhook verification helper in SDKs. Allow per-team webhook secrets and rotate via Console.
sdk_plan: JS + Python: high-level functions: - client.applyRecommendation(recId, {dryRun, canaryFraction, validateRules}, idempotencyKey) - client.waitForOperation(opId, {timeout}) - client.rollbackOperation(opId) - server.verifyWebhook(payload, signature, secret) Implement automatic retries for transient 5xx errors and surface operation links for manual inspection. Ship initial beta JS SDK in 2 sprints, Python in 3 sprints.
observability_and_metrics: Emit metrics: optimize.apply.request, optimize.apply.duration, optimize.apply.rollback.count, optimize.apply.validation.failures, optimize.cost.delta. Link operation traces to Console Rollouts UI. Add dashboard tile showing active operations, average canary failure rate, and cost savings realized by committed applies.
testing_plan: Unit tests for idempotency and snapshot/restore logic. Integration tests: a) dry-run correctness b) canary rollout -> simulated metric regression triggers rollback c) concurrent apply attempts against same scope to validate optimistic locking. Chaos test: simulate control-plane partial outage during apply and ensure auto-rollback or safe-detect and manual-recovery path. E2E with Dedicated test cluster.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal beta): enable API for Redwood autopilot and internal infra teams only; expose Console operation view. Phase 2 (private beta): opt-in customers with Dedicated/private deployments via feature flag. Phase 3 (GA): enable public API and SDKs; add tenant-level guardrails (max canary fraction, approval-required labels).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: bad recommendation causes production regression => Mitigation: default dry-run=true and require explicit canary_fraction>0 for any automated apply; automatic validation with rollback thresholds. Risk: idempotency collisions => Mitigation: require strong idempotency-key (UUID v4) and server validation of payload equality. Risk: secrets leaked for webhooks => Mitigation: restrict rotation, KMS storage, and short-lived event tokens.
